points.text: Traditional MoE is standard upcycling, not a new proposal; sparse upcycling uncited; delta over MergeKit unclear.
'Previously unavailable' claim conflicts with paper's own account of Mergoo and MergeKit.
No evidence BTS/BTX implementations reproduce original papers' behaviour.
Toolkit's per-projection-router BTX may differ from the original BTX design.
Several statements and citations about prior work appear inaccurate.
Minor: 'Acree-AI' typo, Mergoo footnote lacks citation.
Claims about all families, BTS, Traditional MoE, load balancing; only BTX on Gemma3-4B evaluated.
'Successfully reproduced' claim lacks original numbers for comparison.
Dense baselines undefined and capacity not matched.
'Outperform dense baselines' overclaims; 12B dense wins on some averages.
'Previously unavailable' contradicted by related work on Mergoo and MergeKit.
Enhanced English capability claimed without English evaluation; 3x4B worse on Latin.
Splits, tuning and checkpoint selection protocol unstated.
Cost reduction asserted but not measured.
Visualizer excludes BTS, the method called most interpretable.
Dominant expert defined inconsistently between sections.
Presentation slips: duplicated citation, 'Acree-AI', stitch_freq in BTX config.
Routing equation input dimension for down_proj possibly wrong.
Evaluation covers one model, one method, one language pair; other methods and load balancing untested.
No latency, memory, throughput or GPU-hour measurements; cost claims unmeasured.
Single-run results with no seeds or variance; small margins.
Reproduction unverifiable; original Nile-Chat numbers not shown.
Dense baselines undescribed; comparisons not matched in parameters, data or compute.
Key experimental details missing (LoRA, router training, alpha, data, benchmarks, selection).
Component claims (per-projection routers, router-only tuning) lack ablation.
English capability claim untested; 3x4B below 2x4B on Latin.
Minor typos and duplicated citation fragment, stitch_freq in BTX config.
'Previously unavailable' wrong given Mergoo's BTX implementation.
Abstract 'outperform dense baselines' holds only against 4B, not 12B.
Venue fit: library description without research finding or controlled recycling study.
Table 1 columns and underlying benchmarks undefined.
Text and abstract overread Table 1, omitting 3x4B and 12B results.
Contribution list mixes features with claims; 'all model families' undemonstrated.
No summary table of functional differences among Traditional, BTX, BTS.
Minor typos and config slip.
No total parameters, memory or latency; serving cost vs dense unknown.
Regex-based patching fragility untested; no compatibility matrix or tests.
Visualizer value asserted without real diagnostic example; averaging hides layer behaviour.
Visualizer does not support BTS.
No data, licence or provenance statement.
Usefulness of supporting BTX/BTS doubtful; few frontier models use them.
No research-focused efficiency optimization for MoE in the codebase.
Many existing codebases already support MoE training and visualization.
Unclear how to integrate with other training codebases like Megatron.
Training/inference efficiency vs Megatron or other MoE frameworks unknown.
Motivation weak; necessity beyond DeepSpeed-MoE, FairScale, Megatron unexplained.
Contribution is engineering integration without scientific novelty.
Evaluation limited to small-scale code-switching; no large-scale or cross-domain results.
No comparison to strong MoE baselines like Mixtral, DeepSeekMoE, Switch.
No measurement of efficiency, scalability or convergence stability.
Merging compute cost and compatibility issues (tokenizer, heterogeneity) undiscussed; gains marginal.
No comparison with model-merging frameworks like AdapterFusion, LoRAHub, ModelSoup.
Visualization analyses descriptive; no quantitative routing entropy or utilization metrics.
Usability unverifiable; 'proven valuable' claim lacks supporting details.
No reimplementation of original BTX/BTS experiments to show implementation quality.
Section 4 'reimplementation' matches original exactly; not independent evidence.
No comprehensive list of configuration options.
No example adapter file for adding new MoE variant.
Unclear whether Table 1 reproduction was actually achieved.
Should replicate another paper with a different method to show toolkit capabilities.

P.summary: Methods are prior work; Traditional MoE is upcycling, uncited.
'Previously unavailable' claim contradicted by related work.
Most claimed methods, families and features not evaluated.
Nile-Chat reproduction unverifiable without original numbers.
No comparison table among MoE methods.
Implementations not validated against original BTX/BTS papers.

Q.summary: Motivation weak given existing MoE codebases.
Merging cost and compatibility issues undiscussed.
No replication of original BTX/BTS or other papers.
